Geman, H. and Ohana, S. (2009). Forward curves, scarcity and price volatility in oil and natural gas markets. Energy Economics 31(4), 576-585.
sources.data_scope: Direct U.S. oil/natural-gas inventory, forward-curve and volatility evidence over an approximately 15-year database. For natural gas, the forward-curve spread is seasonality-filtered using a 12-month interval between the short and long contract; the working-paper description uses front-month versus 13th-month futures, a one-year U.S. interest rate, and monthly EIA inventory. Natural-gas scarcity is inventory below historical average and the inventory-volatility relation is reported as much stronger in winter.

sources.scope: Source-faithful design uses EIA Henry Hub 1-month futures from January 1995 to July 2021 and historical weather variables including wind speed, temperature and precipitation; New York and Louisiana are reported weather locations. This is not evidence for issued-weather-forecast-vintage inputs. Exact weather-provider identity remains to be verified.
